title: Culture and Heritages in India-II: Sikhism, Islam and Christianity
summary: Guru Nanak, the first Guru and founder (1469–1539), was born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib) near Lahore. 'Sikh' comes from the Sanskrit shishya (disciple). After his spiritual experience in 1496 he travelled with Mardana (a Muslim musician) and Bhai Bala (a Hindu peasant), preaching through kirtans and ragas, and spent his last years at Kartarpur. His hymns were compiled in the Adi Granth; he began sangat (sitting together) and pangat (eating together in the langar or free kitchen). He chose Angad as successor. The ten Gurus: Nanak, Angad, Amardas, Ramdas, Arjan Dev, Hargobind, Har Rai, Harkishan, Tegh Bahadur and Gobind Singh (1666–1708). Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa (the pure) and the five Ks: kesh, kangha, kada, kachcha and kirpan. Teachings: one formless God; reject caste and idolatry and superstition; humility, charity, forgiveness and truthfulness. The holy book is the Guru Granth Sahib.

Takht means 'seat of divine power' and gurudwara 'doorway to the master'. The five Takhts: Sri Akal Takht (Amritsar, founded by Guru Hargobind), Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib (Anandpur, where the Khalsa began), Takht Sri Damdama Sahib (where Guru Gobind Singh completed the Guru Granth Sahib), Takht Sri Hazur Sahib (Nanded on the Godavari, where Guru Gobind Singh died) and Takht Sri Patna Sahib (on the Ganga). Gurudwaras: the Golden Temple at Amritsar (town founded by Guru Ram Das in 1577; Arjan Dev completed the temple; Maharaja Ranjit Singh covered it in gold), Bangla Sahib, Sis Ganj Sahib (Chandni Chowk, where Guru Tegh Bahadur was martyred in 1675), Rakab Ganj, Paonta Sahib (Himachal Pradesh, 'paonta' means feet, dedicated to Guru Gobind Singh), Hemkund Sahib (Uttarakhand, 15,200 ft), Anandpur Sahib (Hola Mohalla), Nankana Sahib and Patna Sahib.

Islam ('peace and submission') is monotheistic and was founded by the Prophet Muhammad at Mecca. In 610 CE, at the age of forty, he received Prophethood. Persecuted for opposing idol worship, he migrated (hijrat) from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE, when the Hijri era begins; he died in 632. The four successors were Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali. Five pillars: belief in one God (Allah), five daily prayers facing Mecca, zakat (alms), fasting in Ramadan and the Hajj. Islam came to India with Arab merchants, then the Turks (Sultanate) and the Mughals (1526). Sufis preached peace and brotherhood; their residences are dargahs and khanqahs, visited on the Urs (death anniversary). Qawwali and Kafi grew from music at dargahs.

Dargahs: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki at Mehrauli, Delhi (Phoolwalon ki Sair, begun in 1812 by Mumtaz Mahal, banned in 1942, revived by Nehru in 1961); Hazratbal at Srinagar on the Dal Lake (the only bulbous-domed mosque in Kashmir, holding the sacred hair of the Prophet); Charar-i-Sharif (tomb of Shaikh Nuruddin Rishi, 32 km from Srinagar); Gesu Daraz (Banda Nawaz) at Gulbarga; Haji Ali at Mumbai in the sea; Sabir Kaliyari at Roorkee; Moinuddin Chishti (Garib Nawaz) at Ajmer, visited October to March with the annual Urs; Nizamuddin Auliya at Delhi (qawwalis, tombs of Amir Khusrau and Jahanara); Nagore Dargah in Tamil Nadu (500 years old, five minarets and a golden dome).

Christianity is based on the teachings of Jesus Christ, who lived in Palestine about 2,000 years ago and chose twelve Apostles (St Peter and St Paul founded churches; their accounts are in the New Testament). St Thomas is believed to have reached Muziris on the western coast and founded the Saint Thomas Christians. The Portuguese brought Francis Xavier (1506–52); Akbar gave freedom to missions. A church is often built in the shape of a cross with the altar facing east; the Bible is the holy book.

Heritage sites: St Thomas Mount (Chennai), San Thomas Basilica (Santhome, Chennai), Velankanni church (the most visited in Tamil Nadu), Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa, 1605, a World Heritage monument holding the relics of St Francis Xavier, exposition every ten years), Se Cathedral and the Church of St Francis of Assisi (Goa), St Cajetan, the Thomas Church at Kodungallur (Kerala), the Presbyterian church at Ross Island (Andamans), the Holy Christ Church (Shimla), St John's Church (McLeod Ganj), Skinner's church (St James, Delhi, 1836), the Sardhana church of Begum Samru (near Meerut; visited in March and November) and Solomon's Temple at Aizawl (Mizoram).

Describe the concept of langar.
A langar is the free kitchen of a gurudwara. People of all castes sit together in pangat to eat, which teaches equality.
Describe the five Ks of Sikhs.
They are kesh (uncut hair), kangha (comb), kada (iron bracelet), kachcha (underwear) and kirpan (sword). They were established by Guru Gobind Singh when he founded the Khalsa.
How did Christianity come to India? Explain in two points.
St Thomas, a disciple of Jesus, is believed to have reached Muziris on the western coast and founded churches. The Portuguese later brought missionaries such as Francis Xavier to the western coast.
What is a dargah? Why is it a tourist attraction?
A dargah is a Sufi shrine built over the grave of a saint, often with a khanqah. It attracts people of all religions, especially on the Urs, with qawwali and fairs.
List the major festivals of Muslims.
Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Zuha (Bakrid), Moharram and Eid Milad-un-Nabi.
Explain 'Takht' in Sikhism.
A takht is the seat of divine power and of social and political decisions of the Gurus. There are five: Akal Takht, Keshgarh, Damdama, Hazur Sahib and Patna Sahib.
Who was Begum Samru? Why is Sardhana famous?

Begum Samru was the Roman Catholic wife of a German mercenary, who commanded his force after his death. She built the beautiful Sardhana church near Meerut, a heritage site visited in March and November.
sa: Explain any three Christian heritage sites located in Tamil Nadu.

(i) St Thomas Mount near Chennai, where St Thomas is believed to have been killed, with a stone cross carved by him. (ii) San Thomas Basilica at Santhome, Chennai, a 16th-century church with stained glass and a statue of Virgin Mary. (iii) The Velankanni church, the most visited pilgrimage centre of Christians in Tamil Nadu.
Explain the life of Guru Nanak after 1496 (three points).

(i) In 1496 he had an extraordinary spiritual experience. (ii) With Mardana and Bhai Bala he travelled from village to village preaching love and brotherhood through kirtans and ragas. (iii) He spent his last years at Kartarpur and chose Angad as his successor.
Describe the teachings of Guru Nanak in three points.
(i) There is one formless God. (ii) The caste system, idolatry and superstitions should be rejected. (iii) Humility, charity, forgiveness and truthfulness should be practised.
Describe the main features of Islamic culture (three points).

(i) Islam is monotheistic and its five pillars are faith, prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj. (ii) Muslims pray five times a day facing Mecca. (iii) Sufis preached peace and brotherhood and their dargahs and Urs attract all communities.
Explain the importance of the Golden Temple (three points).

(i) The town of Amritsar was founded by Guru Ram Das in 1577 on land gifted by Akbar. (ii) Guru Arjan Dev completed the temple and Maharaja Ranjit Singh covered it with gold, so it is the Swarna Mandir. (iii) It is the most sacred shrine of the Sikhs.
la: Write an essay on the life and teachings of Guru Nanak, in six points.

(i) He was born at Talwandi near Lahore in 1469, the first Guru and a great Bhakti saint. (ii) He learned Sanskrit and Persian and had a spiritual experience in 1496. (iii) With Mardana and Bhai Bala he travelled to spread love and brotherhood through kirtans. (iv) He taught one formless God and rejected caste, idolatry and superstition. (v) He taught humility, charity, forgiveness and truthfulness and began sangat and langar. (vi) His hymns were compiled in the Adi Granth and he chose Angad as successor before dying at Kartarpur (1539).
Describe the most popular Sikh Takhts and Gurudwaras in six points.

(i) Sri Akal Takht, founded by Guru Hargobind. (ii) Keshgarh Sahib, where the Khalsa began, and Damdama Sahib, where Guru Gobind Singh completed the Guru Granth Sahib. (iii) Hazur Sahib at Nanded and Patna Sahib on the Ganga. (iv) The Golden Temple at Amritsar and Bangla Sahib in Delhi. (v) Sis Ganj Sahib, where Guru Tegh Bahadur was martyred in 1675. (vi) Hemkund Sahib at 15,200 ft and Paonta Sahib.
Describe the most popular Islamic heritage sites available to tourists in India, in six points.

(i) Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's dargah at Mehrauli with the Phoolwalon ki Sair. (ii) Nizamuddin dargah in Delhi with qawwalis. (iii) Moinuddin Chishti's dargah at Ajmer with its annual Urs. (iv) Hazratbal and Charar-i-Sharif in Kashmir. (v) Haji Ali in Mumbai and Gesu Daraz at Gulbarga. (vi) Nagore dargah in Tamil Nadu with a golden dome and five minarets.
Describe five important Christian heritage sites in India, in six points.

(i) Basilica of Bom Jesus (Old Goa), with St Francis Xavier's relics. (ii) St Thomas Mount and San Thomas Basilica in Chennai. (iii) Velankanni church in Tamil Nadu. (iv) Thomas Church at Kodungallur in Kerala. (v) Skinner's church in Delhi, the Holy Christ Church in Shimla and the Sardhana church. (vi) The Presbyterian church at Ross Island and Solomon's Temple at Aizawl.
